title: Color Grading in Photoshop: Camera Raw workflow (Day 21 of 30 Days of Photoshop)
summary: This PHLEARN tutorial demonstrates a non-destructive color grading workflow in Photoshop using the Camera Raw filter. The presenter converts the background layer to a smart object, applies a Camera Raw filter as a smart filter, and then uses the Color Grading panel to selectively adjust midtones, shadows, and highlights with Hue/Saturation/Luminance controls. The process emphasizes visual experimentation, a before/after toggle, and blending and balance controls to fine-tune how color grades interact with different tonal ranges. A second sample image is used to show the same workflow in a more romantic, straightforward style. The video also covers re-opening Camera Raw for iterative tweaks and using the filter’s opacity for subtler effects, all within a non-destructive editing setup.
topics: Moody vs romantic color grading styles
Saturation and luminance adjustments in highlights
Color grading as a tonal storytelling tool

sections.title: Intro and setup: Color grading in Photoshop with Camera Raw
sections.description: Introduction to the Day 21 technique: using the Camera Raw filter for color grading and the non-destructive workflow enabled by converting the background layer to a Smart Object and applying a Camera Raw filter as a Smart Filter.

sections.title: Create a smart object and open Camera Raw
sections.description: Convert the background layer to a Smart Object, then apply Filter > Camera Raw Filter. This establishes a non-destructive, editable color grading pipeline.

sections.title: Color Grading panel and three-way controls
sections.description: Explore the Color Grading panel. Use midtones, shadows, and highlights with hue, saturation, and luminance controls. Utilize the heads-up display to tweak values and the eye icon to compare before/after.

sections.title: Blending, balance, and committing changes
sections.description: Use Blending and Balance to prioritize shadows or highlights. Toggle default settings, commit the changes, and note that the Smart Filter remains editable (re-openable) for adjustments.

sections.title: Second example: Color grading O2 and tips
concepts: Global color option and selective color
sections.description: Apply the same Camera Raw color grading workflow to a second image (O2). Discuss preferred color tendencies (cool shadows, warm highlights) and mention the option to apply a global color or keep targeted color in shadows/highlights. Conclude with tips on taking breaks to reassess color grading.
